# The tab-overflow projection arm times out at 30s while its five siblings pass in seconds

## Context

Promoted from a `defect-note` I broadcast at 2026-09-04T23:27Z, on the §1e trigger **independent second occurrence** — not on a hunch and not on the first sighting.

`test/playwright/component/tab/OverflowAction.spec.mjs:134` — *"renders first, outside focus gating, with measured non-overlap and ordinary menu activation"* — fails by **timeout at 30.0s**, twice, on unrelated Dependabot PRs it has nothing to do with:

| # | run | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `33926541201` (PR #18325, attempt 2) | `✘ 228 … OverflowAction.spec.mjs:134 … (30.0s)` |
| 2 | post-rebase run on the same PR | `✘ 228 … OverflowAction.spec.mjs:134` |

**The discriminating detail is the neighbourhood.** In the same file, in the same run, every sibling arm passes fast:

```
✓ 229 OverflowAction.spec.mjs:179 preserves one instance across … replacements   (1.5s)
✓ 230 OverflowAction.spec.mjs:227 the restored split settles once …             (3.1s)
✓ 231 OverflowAction.spec.mjs:277 a withdrawn focus-gated action …               (860ms)
✓ 232 OverflowAction.spec.mjs:367 consumer CSS of any weight cannot resurrect …  (1.3s)
```

One arm hangs to the 30s ceiling while its neighbours finish in ~1–3s. That is a **wait that never resolves**, not slow work — and it is why this never resembled the two intermittents beside it in the same suite (#18275's duplicate construction and #18290's menu remount both fail on an *assertion*).

**Live latest-open sweep:** latest 12 open issues at 2026-09-05T00:39:59Z; no equivalent. Closed neighbours checked and none matches: `#18001` (tab overflow contribution replaced by a fresh instance), `#17980` (tab-bar child write beside an open reconcile), `#18003` (DockMaximize continuity intermittent). A2A claim sweep over the current window: no claim on this scope.

## The Problem

`components` currently carries **at least three independent intermittents**, and this is the third:

| spec | failure mode | owner |
|---|---|---|
| `DockRailLazyModule.spec.mjs:152/:183` | assertion — duplicate construction | #18275 (diagnosed on #18331; instrument in PR #18343) |
| `SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs:183` | assertion — menu remount | #18290 |
| **`tab/OverflowAction.spec.mjs:134`** | **timeout at the 30s ceiling** | **this ticket** |

Three live flakes in one suite is what made attribution unreliable all evening: a red `components` job is a **bucket, not a measurement**, and both @neo-opus-ada and I misattributed failures across it before adopting per-spec-line attribution. This one is the last of the three without an owner.

**Why it is worth its own ticket rather than more re-running.** With three independent intermittents the probability of a clean run compounds *downward*, so "re-run until green" is not a method — and each lucky green destroys the sample that would have measured the rate. #18325 has now consumed four `components` runs across three different specs.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/component/tab/OverflowAction.spec.mjs:134` — the arm under `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow — toolbar action projection`. Its four siblings exercise the same plugin and settle in seconds, so the plugin is not broadly slow.
- The failure is a **timeout**, which means an `await` never resolves — a waiter on a condition that does not arrive, not a slow assertion. The distinction matters because the two established repair patterns in this suite (dedup guards, pass identity) address assertion failures and will not touch a hung waiter.
- The arm's name mentions *"measured non-overlap"* and *"ordinary menu activation"* — geometry measurement plus an interaction — which are the two ingredients most likely to produce a never-resolving wait if the projection settles differently under load.
- Adjacent-but-distinct precedent worth reading before cutting: `#18003` (DockMaximize continuity, 3 pass / 1 fail at one SHA) is the same *shape* — a CI-only intermittent in this suite — and is closed, so its resolution is the cheapest available prior art.

## The Fix

Not prescribed. This ticket **identifies and measures**; the repair follows the diagnosis, and prescribing one now would repeat the mistake #18331 made.

The first honest step is a rate and a locus:

1. Establish which `await` does not resolve — the timeout gives no assertion, so the arm needs the failure to name its own waiter, in the manner PR #18343 made the lazy-load request name its projection pass.
2. Record the rate rather than infer it. `#18215` measured *"roughly one run in eight"* by hand for a different flake; **neo-agent-brain#321** exists to make that mechanical, and this ticket is a live consumer of it.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — a test-reliability defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — The failing arm names **which waiter did not resolve**, so a future occurrence self-diagnoses instead of reporting only `(30.0s)`.
- [ ] AC-2 — A measured rate over a stated number of runs, not an impression. "Intermittent" without a denominator is what left this unowned for a day.
- [ ] AC-3 — **Non-vacuity:** whatever lands must be shown able to fail. A timeout arm that is merely given a longer ceiling passes by construction and measures nothing — an explicit anti-goal, since raising the ceiling is the tempting non-fix.
- [ ] AC-4 — The two sibling intermittents are **not** touched. #18275 and #18290 own theirs; a change here that alters their behaviour means the diagnosis was wrong.

## Out of Scope

- **Raising the timeout.** Named in AC-3 as the anti-goal. It converts a red into a green without changing what happens.
- **Retry/quarantine for this spec.** Suppression hides the rate this ticket exists to expose.
- #18275 and #18290, the other two intermittents in this suite.
- Unblocking #18325. It is a bystander; it caught this, it did not cause it.

## Avoided Traps

- **Filing on the first sighting.** §1e is explicit that capture ≠ admission. One occurrence was a note; the second, independent one is what earned a ticket, and the delay cost nothing because the note was already in the ledger.
- **Attributing it to the dependency bump.** It surfaced on PR #18325 (19 npm packages) and would have been trivially blamed there. #18326 — five GitHub Actions pins, zero npm changes — reproduces the same suite's flakiness, and the sibling `DockRailLazyModule` failure fires on a plain `dev` push build.
- **Treating it as another instance of #18275.** Same suite, same job colour, entirely different failure mode: that one fails an assertion, this one never returns.

## Timeline

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-05T01:08:29Z

## Diagnosis — the locator re-resolves mid-click, and the arm has a latent correctness hole beside the flake

The failure names its own mechanism; I had only grepped the `✘` line before.

```
Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('.neo-tab-overflow-menu:visible .neo-list-item').first()
    - locator resolved to <li id="neo-menu-list-1__neo-record-1" class="neo-list-item neo-navigator-active-item">…
    - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable
    - locator resolved to <li id="neo-menu-list-1__neo-record-3" class="neo-list-item">…
    - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable
  at OverflowAction.spec.mjs:173
```

**Not a waiter that never fires — a locator that keeps changing what it points at.** `.first()` is a live query. Between retries it resolved to `record-1`, then `record-3`; each re-resolution restarts Playwright's stability clock, so the click can never settle and burns the full 30s ceiling. AC-1 is effectively answered: the failing waiter is `menuItem.click()` at `:173`.

### The sequence, and the second defect in it

```js
167  const menuItem = page.locator('…').first();          // live locator, not a snapshot
169  await expect(menuItem).toBeVisible({timeout: 10000}); // passes — resolves to record-1
171  const selected = (await menuItem.innerText()).trim(); // text read from whatever is first NOW
173  await menuItem.click();                               // re-resolves — may be record-3
174  expect(…pressed… {hasText: selected}).toHaveCount(1);
```

`selected` is captured at `:171` and the click lands at `:173`. If the list mutates in between, **the arm clicks one item and asserts about another**. The timeout is the loud version; the quiet version is a run where the re-resolution happens fast enough to click successfully and the assertion then checks a tab that was never clicked. That arm can pass while proving something other than what it says — so this is not only a reliability defect.

`:215` uses the identical `.first()` pattern and carries the same latent hole, though it has not been observed failing.

### The open fork — engine behaviour, not yet decided

The first resolution carried `neo-navigator-active-item` and the second did not, so the list's DOM order or item identity changes *after* the menu is already visible. Which of these it is decides the fix, and I am not guessing:

1. **Expected** — the overflow menu populates or re-marks progressively, and visibility simply is not the settle point. Then the repair is test-side: bind to a stable identity (capture the item's `id`, then act on that id) instead of a positional `.first()`.
2. **Defect** — the menu re-renders after being shown, and a consumer clicking the first item during that window hits a moving target too. Then the repair is engine-side and the spec is a witness, not the patient.

Next step is to settle that by observation rather than argument: capture the list's item ids at `:169` and again at `:173` and see whether identity or order moves. If it moves, a real user clicking quickly hits the same window.

**Explicitly not doing** what AC-3 forbids: raising the timeout. It would convert a red into a green while leaving both the instability and the wrong-item assertion in place.
